dossier.architecture: Bump-only, very large-capacity four-wide drum robot.

subsystems.drivetrain: Custom wide-wheel swerve with easily changed ratios; lower gearing chosen for fully loaded bump travel.
subsystems.intake: Five-ball-wide pickup with dual-X60 roller; added shielding prevents hopper load from stalling collector.
subsystems.transfer: Large roller floor and shaped entry preserve flow; hopper structure revised from angle to tubing for stiffness.
subsystems.scoring: Four-wide preaccelerated drum; passive PVC guide and grip tape improved consistency. Two-position hood changed from pneumatic to linear actuation; speed fills remaining range.
subsystems.endgame: Endgame installation not established in reviewed interview.
subsystems.controls: Driver practice focused on sweeping moving/dispersed fuel; source contrasts regional piles with more mobile Worlds supply.

versions: Team reports roughly 115-fuel capacity and 20 BPS; these are reported configuration measurements, not independent match-rate measurements.
dossier.analysis: The big-hopper choice can be coherent when loaded travel remains quick and fuel access is adequate. Model loaded mass and route contestability; holding more fuel is not useful if bump defense prevents reaching a scoring window.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2026-2481 · Large inventory changes collector loading, frame clearance and drive gearing
context_documents.body:
# 2026-2481: Large inventory changes collector loading, frame clearance and drive gearing

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The interview reports approximately 115-fuel capacity, a 33.5×21.375-inch robot envelope before the described extension, a wide 3-inch two-X60 intake, a load shield above the collector, and hopper structure changed from angle to tube. A two-position hood changed from pneumatic to linear actuation; wheel speed covers intermediate distances. Custom modules allow ratio changes and were geared down for the loaded robot.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The second collector motor and load shield respond to stalling and hopper pressure. Tube structure responds to racking and snagging. The lower drive ratio is explicitly tied to moving a heavily loaded robot across bumps with less stalling/current; the source attributes the actuator change to weight.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Capacity is useful only if it remains mobile and unloads reliably. A large stored column presses on its lowest contact surfaces, so a shield can be more valuable than another nominally faster roller. The hopper bar cutout and wheel sizing belong to the same route-clearance problem: a robot that can collect a full load but beaches on the bump loses the strategic value of that load. Two hood positions simplify mechanism travel, but the remaining range must be supplied by speed without creating unacceptable release-angle or recovery-time sensitivity.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test acceleration, bump traversal, braking, tip margin and current at empty/half/full inventory. Measure sustained unload rate rather than dividing nominal capacity by the fastest initial volley. Verify exact dimensions and the source gear notation in CAD.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=phBgiNvrYCc](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=phBgiNvrYCc)

source_reviews.title: Team 2481 Roboteers interview
source_reviews.locator: 0:43–1:38 launcher; 2:23–4:16 collector; 4:34–6:34 storage and floor; 6:48–9:13 driving and practice
source_reviews.review_basis: Read available English captions of the team interview. Times refer to the source video.
facts: The team added a collector motor after stalls and changed wall supports after catches and racking.
Bump-only travel and loaded gearing were part of the scoring strategy.
source_reviews.limitations: Reported 20 BPS and 115 fuel are team claims. The interview does not establish independent capacity or full-match throughput.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Roboteers built a large fuel carrier whose value depended on unloading a useful batch through a wide shooter. The robot traded the trench route for more volume and took the bump with that load. Its collector, hopper walls, feeder and wheel gearing therefore belong in the same design decision. An empty sprint or a bench burst would leave the difficult parts of the architecture untested.
piece_flow: The wide roller gathers fuel while a relief plate reduces direct bulk pressure on the collector.
Fuel fills the deployable volume and settles onto interlocking floor rollers.
The floor and serial contact stages move fuel into four launch lanes. The top contact conditions fuel entry without requiring another driven roller in that position.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The team describes a relatively narrow chassis dimension that makes the direction of bump crossing matter. The larger loaded footprint comes from extending walls. Heavy hardware sits low, but fuel raises the combined center of mass and can surge as the robot starts up the bump. The route must be wide enough to cross on a repeatable heading even when a defender approaches.

subsystems.name: Collector and pressure relief
subsystems.construction: Three-inch grip-covered intake roller with two motors in the reported later setup. A plate limits fuel weight pressing directly on the intake.
subsystems.operation: Keep the intake running while fuel accumulates just inside the mouth.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team added the second motor after stall problems.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Separate lack of available torque from an unfavorable contact load. A pressure barrier can prevent bulk inventory from continuously loading a roller intended to accelerate one layer at a time.
subsystems.interfaces: The roller opening must stay useful across a wide mouth while walls retract and extend.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: A pressure-relief feature can become a pinch point if fuel wedges under it. Test new and worn balls while pushing against a full bin.
subsystems.unknowns: Precise gaps, currents and endurance data are unresolved.

subsystems.name: Expanding hopper and floor
subsystems.construction: Flexible side structure and a roller floor feed the four-wide launch section. The team revised wall support geometry.
subsystems.operation: Deploy the hopper for bulk collection. The floor presents lower fuel while the rest of the load settles.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team changed supports after racking and catches.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: More static volume gives diminishing returns if the added fuel bridges above the floor, spills during travel or takes longer than the active scoring window to clear.
subsystems.interfaces: The floor must coexist with electronics and route-clearance requirements. The stowed wall envelope sets bump clearance and access to the drivetrain.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Measure load retention over repeated crossings and examine where a bent wall first intrudes into the roller path.
subsystems.unknowns: The 115-fuel estimate is a source claim under unspecified packing conditions.

subsystems.name: Four-wide launcher
subsystems.construction: Multiple accelerator contacts feed a wide launch assembly. A passive upper contact and electric hood actuation are described.
subsystems.operation: Build fuel speed over successive contacts, then launch at the selected angle and flywheel speed.
subsystems.team_rationale: The extra upper contact improved the entrance without adding a powered roller in that location.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: If launch contact force varies by lane, equal speed commands do not imply equal release speed or trajectory. Measure misses by lane and shooter speed recovery during a full burst.
subsystems.interfaces: The floor and shooter need equal flow across the width. A single loaded lane can reduce consistency even if the motor has ample total power.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Bracket repairs and actuator changes show the value of replacing a high-load mounting point without rebuilding the floor.
subsystems.unknowns: Reported BPS lacks a confirmed measurement window and scoring conversion rate.

subsystems.name: Loaded drivetrain and routes
subsystems.construction: The team describes custom adjustable-gearing swerve, large wheels and a chassis shaped to cross the bump.
subsystems.operation: Approach in the planned direction, climb the obstacle loaded and return to a scoring position.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team chose gearing for loaded current and the crossing rather than maximum possible speed.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Compare the obstacle route with the alternative under realistic traffic. More fuel per trip can still lose if repeated turns, beaching or queueing consume the scoring window.
subsystems.interfaces: Drive tuning, fuel retention and the approach geometry are coupled. Electrical demand rises when the drivetrain and feeder operate together.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test from a partially discharged battery and a poor entry angle. The team credited practice as well as mechanical changes.
subsystems.unknowns: No controlled timing across routes, configurations and driver practice levels.

revisions: Collector changed from one motor to two after stalling.
Hopper support geometry revised after catches and racking.
Electric hood actuator replaced a pneumatic approach in the reported configuration.
transferable_principles: Test a loaded route before choosing gearing or capacity.
Keep intake roller force separate from hopper inventory where practical.
Compare scored fuel per complete cycle, including travel, stalled feeds and misses.
disconfirming_conditions: The trench route can reverse the capacity trade if it removes enough defense exposure or travel time.
A smaller hopper can match effective output when the active window or the feeder sets the limit.
remaining_gaps: No independent match-by-match cycle sample or controlled comparison of shooter configurations.
